full_judgment:
6. Mr. Md. Nurullah, learned Counsel for the petitioners reiterates the submissions made unsuccessfully before the High Court Division, namely, that the petition will fail for misjoinder of causes of action because respondent No. 1 ought to have filed 5 separate cases for pre-emption of 5 kabalas of different dates, the sellers being different and the purchasers being different and that the pre-emption case is barred by limitation. 

 "99. No decree shall be reversed or substantially varied, nor shall any case be remanded, in appeal on account of any misjoinder of parties or causes of action or any error, defect or irregularity in any proceedings in the suit, not affecting the merits of the case or the jurisdiction of the Court."
